Maruszow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Markuszów, Poland

Demolished. Markuszów's Jewish community, though individual Jewish residents are documented from the first half of the 17th century, was only formally established toward its end. This small cemetery — just 0.03 hectares, based on a 1922 map — stood beside the synagogue and was replaced by a newer cemetery in the first quarter of the 19th century; before WWII it was already overgrown, though several matzevot remained. It is unclear whether those last tombstones disappeared during the war — possibly in the September 1939 bombing that also destroyed a newer synagogue nearby — or sometime after. In the 1970s, the site was redeveloped into a building now housing the Commune Office, Community Center, and Fire Department; no evidence of the cemetery survives today.
